Eggs of the meagre Argyrosomus regius are pelagic and spherical, with a measured diameter of 0.1056 centimeters . This relatively small oocyte size is typical of sciaenids that spawn in coastal waters, where the high surface area to volume ratio facilitates rapid oxygen diffusion during early development. The freshly fertilised ovum weighs approximately 0.000718 grams [Ww0 = approximately 0.000718 grams], reflecting the modest yolk reserves that characterise this species. When incubated at a stable temperature of 22 °C [T = 22 °C], chorion rupture and larval eclosion occur after just 1 day . The newly emerged yolk-sac larva, or prolarva, measures 0.295 centimeters  in total length at hatch and remains entirely lecithotrophic, subsisting on its endogenous yolk supply. The transition to exogenous feeding is closely tied to the complete resorption of the yolk sac, a critical juncture that typically coincides with mouth opening and the onset of active prey detection.

Following yolk absorption under the same thermal regime of 22 °C [T = 22 °C], the free-swimming larva begins exogenous feeding and grows rapidly. The period of endogenous nutrition, from chorionase secretion to yolk depletion, spans just 1 day  after fertilisation at a temperature of 22 °C [T = 22 °C]. By approximately 35 days  after hatching, the larva undergoes a pronounced morphological transformation characterised by fin ray ossification and scale formation onset, marking the larval-juven at a temperature of 22 °C [T = 22 °C]ile transition. At this metamorphic climax, the individual is classified as a post-metamorphic juvenile with a total length at metam of 3.2 centimeters . This size represents a substantial increase from the 0.295 centimeter  length at hatch, indicating a period of rapid somatic growth. The metamorphosed fish then becomes a benthic juvenile, shifting from a pelagic existence to demersal habitats.

Growth continues through the juvenile and sub-adult stages, and the ultimate total length attained by this species is considerable, reaching an asymptotic value of 230 centimeters [Li = 230 centimeters]. The corresponding ultimate wet weight, representing the maximum recorded body mass in adults, is 103 kilograms [Wwi = 103 kilograms]. These values position Argyrosomus regius as one of the larger members of the family Sciaenidae, with a body size that facilitates piscivorous predation in coastal and estuarine environments. In a comparative context, the asymptotic size of 230 centimeters [Li = 230 centimeters] rivals that of its congener Argyrosomus japonicus, though growth rates may differ regionally. Laboratory-based studies conducted at 20 °C [T = 20 °C] reported a gonadosomatic index (GSI) of 5% [GSI = 5%] for reproductively active females during the pre-spawning period.

Sexual maturation in Argyrosomus regius is a gradual process, with the total length at puberty, typically corresponding to the onset of gonad maturation, recorded at 80 centimeters [Lp = 80 centimeters]. The corresponding wet weight at puberty for females at this size is approximately 5 kilograms [Wwp = approximately 5 kilograms]. Under ambient thermal conditions averaging 18 °C [T = 18 °C], field surveys and long-term monitoring of tagged individuals indicate that the first spawning event typically occurs at 4 years after hatching [tR = 4 years after hatching]. This age at first reproduction is consistent with a moderately late-maturing sciaenid that invests in somatic growth before diverting resources toward gametogenesis. In contrast, the lifespan of this species is considerably longer; the oldest documented individuals, when maintained at 18 °C [T = 18 °C], have been recorded reaching approximately 15 years [am = approximately 15 years]. This maximum longevity of 15 years [am = 15 years] aligns with the life-history strategy of a relatively large, iteroparous teleost at a temperature of 18 °C [T = 18 °C].

At a rearing temperature of 22 °C [T = 22 °C], the age at first exogenous feeding, marked by complete yolk-sac resorption, is 4 days [ab = 4 days]. The total length at birth, measured as the standard length immediately following this transition, is 0.362 centimeters [Lb = 0.362 centimeters], which is notably greater than the 0.295 centimeter  length recorded at the moment of hatching because the initially curled prolarva straightens upon emergence. The wet weight at birth for these newly feeding individuals is 0.00037 grams [Wwb = 0.00037 grams], a value that declines slightly from the egg wet weight of 0.000718 grams [Ww0 = 0.000718 grams] as yolk is catabolised. This rapid succession of developmental events underscores the necessity of elevated temperatures for successful larval rearing in aquaculture settings. Juveniles recruit to demersal habitats along the continental shelf, where they transition to a piscivorous diet and continue their growth toward the impressive adult dimensions typical of this pelagic sciaenid.
